summary: Batch-size economics was the single biggest lever in this cell: at the shipped shape, 2^19 -> 2^18 tokens/step gained 0.0094 bpb (0.997359 -> 0.987984, commit d3c56c2) and on a2's depth-8/dim-640 base a further move to 197K tokens/step (DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE=96, grad_accum=1, LRs unchanged) gained another 0.0044 to 0.979464 (9aed73d), the best result I measured. Three things in my family did not work: 2^17 with micro-batch 64 (1.004693), training at seq_len 1024 with eval at 2048 (1.003736, train/eval context mismatch costs ~0.016), and a batch-size ramp 131K->262K->524K (0.987048 vs 0.985426 for the fixed batch on the same shape). Stacking the peer width win (dim 640 -> 768) on top of my 197K batch gave 0.979760 -- a wash, so the width and batch gains overlap rather than add. Next I would sweep batch between 131K and 197K at fixed micro-batch efficiency (e.g. 80 and 112 rows, accum 1) with a small sqrt-scaled LR adjustment, since the optimum clearly sits below 2^18 and the shape gains appear to be mostly the same degree of freedom.
